skill.name: azure-communication-sms-java
skill.description: Guides Java developers through sending SMS with Azure Communication Services, including client setup, single and bulk sends, async operations, delivery reports, and error handling.
skill.summary: Implement Azure Communication Services SMS messaging in Java.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static command execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline formatting. The hardcoded URL and system reconnaissance findings are also false positives because they document Azure SDK configuration and SMS delivery handling. One low-severity semantic issue remains: sample logging can expose recipient phone numbers and SMS metadata.

remediation.issue: Logging examples expose SMS recipient data and metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Update examples to redact phone numbers, message IDs, headers, and detailed error bodies before logging.

remediation.issue: Bulk and marketing SMS examples lack consent and opt-out guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for consent records, opt-out handling, sender registration, and rate limits before bulk sending.

remediation.issue: Credential examples include connection string and access key placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Emphasize DefaultAzureCredential first and warn users never to commit connection strings or access keys.

content.user_title: Build Azure SMS Messaging in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams often need SMS flows without memorizing Azure SDK calls. This skill gives focused patterns for clients, sends, errors, and reports.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency configuration for azure-communication-sms 1.2.0.
Demonstrates client creation with DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, and AzureKeyCredential.
Covers single recipient, bulk recipient, and async send flows.
Explains SmsSendOptions for delivery reports and tracking tags.
Shows response handling, HTTP status checks, and per-recipient error handling.
Lists required environment variables for endpoints, connection strings, and sender numbers.
limitations: Requires an Azure Communication Services resource, phone number, and valid credentials.
Does not include a complete Spring Boot or servlet application.
Delivery report handling is only described at a placeholder level.
Does not implement consent management, opt-out handling, or SMS compliance controls.

use_cases.title: Add verification messages

use_cases.title: Send operational alerts
use_cases.description: Create SMS notifications for incidents, order updates, and service events.

use_cases.title: Track delivery outcomes
use_cases.description: Plan delivery report handling with Event Grid and message tags.

prompt_templates.title: Send one SMS
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single recipient message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-communication-sms-java skill to outline a Java flow for sending one SMS with DefaultAzureCredential. Include configuration, send result checks, and basic errors.

prompt_templates.title: Create bulk notifications
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate flow for sending to several recipients.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-communication-sms-java skill to design a bulk SMS notification flow in Java. Include recipient lists, SmsSendOptions, delivery reports, and per-recipient failures.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate delivery reports
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for tracking delivery status.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-communication-sms-java skill to plan delivery report tracking for Azure Communication Services SMS. Cover Event Grid setup, message tags, status storage, and retry decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Review production readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for reliability and security.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-communication-sms-java skill to review a Java SMS service for production readiness. Check credential handling, retries, rate limits, consent, opt-out handling, and log redaction.

output_examples.input: Create a one-time password SMS flow in Java.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with dependency setup, DefaultAzureCredential client creation, sender and recipient configuration, send result checks, and retry guidance.

output_examples.input: Add delivery report tracking to my SMS service.
output_examples.output: A design outline that connects delivery report options, message tags, Event Grid events, status storage, and customer support lookup needs.

output_examples.input: Review SMS error handling before launch.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering per-recipient failures, invalid numbers, rate limits, request exceptions, and redacted diagnostic logs.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential when possible and store secrets outside source control.
Validate E.164 phone numbers before sending messages.
Redact phone numbers, message IDs, headers, and error bodies in logs.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode access keys, connection strings, or sender numbers in source files.
Do not send bulk or marketing SMS without documented consent and opt-out handling.
Do not treat HTTP success as per-recipient success; inspect each SmsSendResult.

faq.question: Does this skill send SMS messages by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Java code that uses Azure Communication Services SMS.

faq.question: Which Azure authentication methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, and AzureKeyCredential client setup patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with bulk SMS?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows recipient lists, SmsSendOptions, delivery reports, and per-recipient result handling.

faq.question: Does it include delivery report processing?
faq.answer: It explains Event Grid delivery reports, but the webhook parser is only a placeholder.

faq.question: Does it handle SMS compliance requirements?
faq.answer: No. You must add consent records, opt-out handling, sender rules, and regional compliance checks.
